findings.title: Salesforce: `prisma` is used but never imported
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update` is called, but the file has no `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma"`. This fails type-check, and at runtime it throws a ReferenceError every time a Salesforce client is created.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh bypasses credential sync and runs on every client construction
findings.body: The new refresh `fetch` calls Salesforce directly and does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential syncing is ignored for this app. It also fires on every service construction, not only when the token is expired. The refreshed `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token` is then discarded: the Connection is built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token`.

findings.title: Computed zod keys produce a broken schema
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the string "[object Object]" (or similar), not a wildcard. The resulting schema only requires `access_token` plus a literal junk key. Because `z.number()` is required on that junk key, every sync-mode response fails validation, and extra properties are not allowed through as intended.

findings.title: Fake refresh_token is injected into all parsed responses
findings.body: If `refresh_token` is missing, it is set to the literal string "refresh_token", even in the normal non-sync path. That bogus value can then be saved over a real refresh token in the DB. The type of `data` is also not guaranteed to have this property.

findings.title: Parse result object saved as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a safeParse result (`{success, data}`), but it is stored directly as `key`. The credential key becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` and the stored Google credentials are corrupted. The old code stored the parsed data.

findings.title: Sync response is a fetch Response, but code reads `.data`
findings.body: In sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch `Response`, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. The Google path only works when sync is disabled. The same mismatch affects the hubspot, zoho-bigin and zohocrm callers, which expect a JSON or axios-shaped result.

findings.title: Sync endpoint call is unauthenticated and has no error handling
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends no secret or auth header, and the response status is not checked. The caller will try to parse an error body as tokens.

findings.title: Webhook secret compared with `!==` and body errors unhandled
findings.body: The secret is compared with a non-constant-time `!==`. `schema.parse` throws on a bad body, which gives a 500 instead of a 400. `JSON.parse` of the decrypted keys, or decryption itself, can also throw unhandled. There is no method check either.

findings.title: Bigin passes credentialId as userId
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects `userId`, but `credentialId` is passed. The sync endpoint will receive the wrong id for `calcomUserId`.
